unit.title: Emotions and habits
unit.description: Fear, greed, revenge and overtrading: rules so they don't decide for you

texts: Live through Black Monday, 1987
June 1987. You have **€10,000** in the S&P 500 for many years from now. Real data, day by day. You can sell whenever you like.
Go all the way to the end, whether you sell or not.

On 19 October 1987 it fell **20.5 %** in a single day, the biggest one-day fall in its history, and in less than two years it was back at its high. **The moment of greatest fear is usually the moment of greatest opportunity**, and panic asks for exactly the opposite.
You've sold. See what happens next…
The news is all about panic. Can you hold on?
You're already above what you put in.
Hit start. You can sell whenever you like
You're falling behind
Sergio
November 2021. Bitcoin is at record highs and it's all over the news.
I've already doubled what I put in!
You're still not in? You're falling behind.
What do you do?
Put all my savings in before it goes up more
That's greed and FOMO right at the peak.
Stick to my plan and my speculation limit
Nice! If anything goes in, it's the small part you could afford to lose entirely.
Take out a loan to go in big
Debt at the height of euphoria: the worst possible combination.
Bitcoin fell by close to **75 %** over the following year.
The moment of greatest euphoria is usually the moment of **greatest risk**.

steps.title: The emotional cycle
steps.body:
Optimism → excitement → **euphoria** (peak risk) → anxiety → denial → fear → **panic and capitulation** (peak opportunity) → despondency → hope…

It's not about calling the top or the bottom: nobody does that reliably. It's about not letting fear or greed change a plan written while you were calm.
steps.key: Investors tend to buy in euphoria and sell in panic: exactly the opposite of what makes sense.
steps.tip: Try it: set a drop alert on your ETF and decide today what you'll do.

texts: Three losses before lunch
Ana
Three losses in a row this morning. All within my plan.
I'm fuming. I can see another opportunity and I'm going in with triple the size.
What do you tell Ana?
Go on, get your revenge
That's **revenge trading**: if it fails, she loses a month's worth in one afternoon.
Stop for today and come back tomorrow with your normal size
That's it! Three losses are a normal streak. What's not normal is letting anger do the trading.
Remove the stops so they stop getting hit
Without a stop, the next loss has no limit.
The market doesn't know you've lost. It doesn't owe you anything.
OK. I'm switching off the screen and noting it in my journal.
What anger asks for
A **€10,000** account. After three losses of **€100**, anger wants you to risk **€600** on the next one.
If that fourth trade also goes wrong, how much have you lost today in total?
3 × 100 + 600 = **€900**: 9 % of the account in one afternoon. Stopping after the third, it would have been €300.
Go back to your plan's risk: 1 % per trade.
**The risk per trade is always the same**, win or lose. After a loss, the next trade has the same odds as if you'd just won.
This way, win or lose, the risk is always the same.
At this risk, 10 losses in a row take 40 % or more.
Lower the risk to what your plan says

steps.title: The ready-made rule
steps.body:
**«After 3 losses in a row, I stop for the rest of the day.»**

And also:
• The risk per trade is always the same.
• If you lose 6 % in a month, you stop until the next month.
• You note down in your journal how you were feeling.
steps.key: After a loss, the best decision is often to make no more that day.
steps.tip: Try it: check your history and see what you did right after your last loss.

texts: 20 trades a week
Bruno
I make 20 trades a week. If I don't trade, I don't earn.
My journal says I almost break even before costs… and lose after them.
What should Bruno change?
Trade even more to make up for it
More trades, more costs. The hole gets bigger.
Keep only the few that meet his plan
That's it! Fewer trades, better chosen, and costs stop eating everything up.
Switch to something more volatile
More volatility doesn't give you an edge: it just makes the losses bigger.
Do his sum: 20 trades a week is more than **1,000 a year**, and each one pays commission and *spread*.
To make money, he first has to win back all those tolls. You already saw in «Overconfidence» what happens to those who trade the most.
Every trade pays a toll
Simulation: 1,000 people trade **with no edge at all**, like tossing a coin. Every trade pays **€6** in commission and spread. Raise the number of trades.
With 104 trades (2 a week for a year), how much has each person paid in costs?
About €60
About €600
About €6,000
104 × €6 = **€624**, win or lose. Luck is shared out; costs are not.
Raise the number of trades until 3 out of 4 are losing.
**Trading a lot means paying costs again and again.** With no edge, the more trades, the more people end up losing: the cost is the only sure thing.
Three out of four losing, and only because of costs.
Look at the average: every trade takes a little off.
Raise each person's number of trades

steps.title: Your takeaway
steps.body:
The more you watch the market, the more moves you see that mean nothing, and each one seems to call for a decision.

Fewer trades, better chosen, with low costs. And for the long term: automatic contributions and reviewing your portfolio now and then, not every day.
steps.key: Every trade pays costs: trading a lot turns a small edge into a loss.
steps.tip: Try it: keep only the assets in your plan in Favourites and remove the rest.

texts: Buying today?
Before every purchase, a checklist: plan, reason in three sentences, three reasons you could be wrong, stop, size, calm and «would I buy it if nobody were talking about it?».
Not buying today
The checklist says go
I can't explain the reason without saying «because it's going up»
«Because it's going up» isn't a reason: it's FOMO.
I don't know where I'd put the stop
Without a set stop, you don't know how much you're risking.
I've just lost three trades and I'm angry
When you're angry, the checklist says «not today».
It's in my plan, I know my stop, the size fits and I'm calm
If everything is «yes», the checklist lets you trade.
Everyone's talking about it, but without that I wouldn't buy it
If you only want it because people are talking about it, that's herd behaviour.
I've written three reasons I could be wrong and it still ticks every box
You've looked at the other side and the idea holds up: go ahead, with your usual size.
Run the checklist on the six situations.
The checklist only works if you go through it **beforehand and in full**. **If any answer is «no», don't buy today.**
Hint: a single «no» is enough to wait.
Buy or wait? Run the checklist
Six out of seven
Pablo
I've run the checklist: all «yes»… except the calm question.
I'm euphoric: I've won two trades in a row.
What does Pablo do?
Buys anyway: 6 out of 7 is pretty good
One «no» is enough to wait. That question is there for a reason.
Doesn't buy today and reviews it calmly tomorrow
That's it! If it still makes sense tomorrow, the checklist will give 7 out of 7.
Buys double: he's on a roll
Euphoria plus a bigger size: textbook overconfidence.
Pilots use checklists even though they know how to fly.

steps.title: Monthly review
steps.body:
• Have I followed my plan? On which trades not, and why?
• Does my return beat a comparable index?
• Which bias have I spotted in myself this month?

And ask Lumi in Biases mode: Lumi will play devil's advocate.
steps.key: You can't get rid of your emotions; you can stop them deciding for you.
steps.tip: Try it: go through the whole checklist before your next simulator buy.

u28l1-1.prompt: Put this part of the market's emotional cycle in order.
u28l1-1.explanation: Peak risk is in euphoria; peak opportunity, in panic.

u28l1-2.prompt: This is how the S&P 500 was doing during the covid crash. Tap the day of peak panic (the lowest close). (S&P 500 · daily closes · up to 25/03/2020)
u28l1-2.explanation: That March 2020 bottom was the worst time to sell: the index took about 5 months to get back to its high.

u28l1-4.prompt: Real chart of a fall. What trend do you see? (Amazon · closes every 3 sessions · December 2025 – February 2026)
u28l1-4.explanation: Lower highs and lower lows: this is fear territory, where most people sell without a plan.

u28l1-7.prompt: At which stage of the cycle is the risk usually highest?
u28l1-7.explanation: When everyone is in and nobody sees any risks, prices are usually higher than their value justifies.

u28l1-9.prompt: Match each moment in a trade with its typical emotion.
options: The trade is going against you
u28l1-9.explanation: Knowing the emotion of each moment lets you prepare the rule in advance.
right: Anger, the urge to win it back

options: Raising your risk because «I'm on a roll»
Getting into something that's up 200 % so you don't miss out
Removing the stop because «it can't fall any further»
Selling everything after an alarming headline
Closing a small gain out of panic about giving it back
u28l1-10.explanation: Both emotions push you to break your plan, in opposite directions.

options: Your size doesn't depend on what you lost yesterday: stick to your fixed risk
Good idea, you're on a roll now
u28l2-4.explanation: Forcing yourself to win back losses is the quickest way to make them bigger.
feedback: Leverage only speeds up whatever happens, and haste usually makes it bad.
OK. If my system has an edge, it recovers with time, not with haste.
Making €50 doesn't change the odds of the next trade.
lines: Yesterday I lost €300 and today I've made back €50 😌
If I raise my size, I'll win it all back this afternoon.

u28l2-6.prompt: Put in order what to do after three losses in a row.
options: Check whether the trades followed the plan
Come back another day at normal size
Note in your journal what happened and how you felt
u28l2-6.explanation: First cut it off, then record, then analyse and, finally, come back without changing your risk.

u28l2-8.prompt: Which signs show you're revenge trading? Select all that apply.
options: You follow your plan with your usual risk
You raise your size to win it back
You go in without your signal being met
u28l2-8.explanation: Following the plan with your usual risk is exactly the opposite.

u28l2-9.prompt: Ready-made rule: after ____ losses in a row, I stop for the rest of the day.
u28l2-9.explanation: It's the textbook rule: it cuts off the spiral before it grows.

u28l2-10.prompt: What do revenge trading and loss aversion have in common?
options: They both make us take on more risk to avoid accepting a loss
u28l2-10.explanation: When we're losing, we become more reckless: «I'll double up to win it back».

options: Buying because a video says «it's going to explode today»
Switching funds every month to whichever rose most
Selling because the portfolio is down 1 % today
Rebalancing once a year according to the plan
u28l3-8.explanation: Useful decisions come from the plan; noise comes from the screen.

u28l3-9.prompt: Match each cost with its description.
u28l3-9.explanation: They all grow with the number of trades.
right: The difference between the buying and selling price
What you pay Hacienda (the Spanish tax authority) on your gains
The daily cost of holding a leveraged position
What the broker charges per trade

options: Careful: more triggers usually lead to more trades and more costs
u28l3-10.explanation: You don't need to see every move: you need to act only when your plan says so.
feedback: More alerts usually bring more impulsive trades… and more costs.
You're right. I'll keep alerts only for my stops and targets, and check the rest calmly.
lines: I've set up price alerts on 40 shares 📲
That way I won't miss a thing.

u28l3-11.prompt: Your long-term index fund drops 1 % on a Tuesday. You've been opening the app every hour for three days. What do you do?
options: I switch to the fund that's rising most today
I leave it alone: I keep up my contributions and check it now and then
I sell today and buy back when it falls further
u28l3-11.explanation: For the long term, a bad day calls for no decision: every extra trade pays costs and rarely improves the result. The temptation is to «do something» because you're watching.
feedback: Switching to whatever rises today is chasing noise, and every switch pays costs.
Good: 1 % in a day is noise for a plan spanning years.
You pay costs twice and have to get two moments right. You'll usually miss one.

u28l3-12.prompt: What do you pay again every time you buy or sell? Tick all that apply.
options: The spread between the buying and selling price
Taxes, if you sell at a profit
u28l3-12.explanation: Commission, spread and taxes are paid on every trade: that's why trading a lot eats up a small edge. The index's return isn't a cost: it's what you earn if you stay put.

u28l4-1.prompt: Put your anti-bias routine for a trade in order.
options: Every month: review your stats and compare yourself with an index
On exit: note it in your journal
On entry: set your stop and size
During: don't move the stop against you
u28l4-1.explanation: Each moment has its rule: that way emotions can't find a way in.

u28l4-2.prompt: Which questions are on the pre-purchase checklist? Select all that apply.
options: How much has it gone up this week?
Do I know where my stop is?
u28l4-2.explanation: How much it's gone up feeds FOMO, not the decision.

u28l4-4.prompt: Lumi asks you to go through the checklist. What do you reply?
options: Question 7: would you buy it if nobody were talking about it?
Buy half now and go through the checklist later
u28l4-4.explanation: The checklist only works if you go through it beforehand and in full.
feedback: Hmm… honestly, no. So I'm not buying today.
The checklist comes before buying: afterwards it's no use.
When it's «crystal clear» and you're in a hurry is exactly when you need the checklist most.
lines: I want to buy this share right now 🏃

u28l4-5.prompt: What do you tell her in the monthly review?
options: If you made money, breaking the plan doesn't matter
Review those 4 trades: what made you break it and how did they turn out?
u28l4-5.explanation: The monthly review looks at the process, not just the result.
feedback: Winning while breaking the plan teaches you to break it. One day it'll cost you.
Good idea. Two were FOMO and one was revenge. I'll note them down as my biases of the month.
That's overconfidence after a good month.
lines: But I broke the plan on 4 trades…

u28l4-6.prompt: Match each bias with its antidote.
u28l4-6.explanation: Every bias has a specific rule that keeps it in check.
right: Decide from today, ignoring what's been lost
Track it in your journal and compare yourself with an index

u28l4-9.prompt: Which monthly review question tells you whether your active management is worth it?
options: How many trades have I made?
Does my return beat a comparable index?
How long have I spent looking at the screen?
u28l4-9.explanation: If you don't beat the index over several years, buying the index would have served you better.

u28l4-10.prompt: If any answer on the checklist is «no», ____ buy today.
u28l4-10.explanation: Waiting a day hardly ever costs you; buying without going through the checklist often does.
